description: Switch the Morgan featurizer from bit-vector to count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, same radius-2 generator folded to 2048 bins) so repeated substructures contribute their multiplicity, with the RandomForest settings unchanged.
Replace the Morgan fingerprint featurizer with 167-bit MACCS keys (MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) as the only molecular representation, leaving the random forest settings unchanged.
Replace the MACCS random forest with a CatBoost MAE-loss regressor (depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations) on Morgan count fingerprints concatenated with RDKit descriptors.

Replace the CatBoost model with a Tanimoto-kernel ridge regressor on binary Morgan fingerprints, choosing alpha from {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by inner 5-fold GroupKFold on Murcko scaffolds, then refitting on all training data.
Replace the CatBoost MAE regressor with sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor using quantile loss at alpha=0.5 (median regression) on the existing Morgan-count plus RDKit-descriptor features.

Replace the CatBoost regressor with an sklearn MLPRegressor (256,128 hidden, alpha=1e-2, early stopping) and z-score the RDKit descriptor block with a train-fitted StandardScaler clipped to ±5, leaving the Morgan bits unscaled.

Replace the Morgan count fingerprint with hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair generator, 2048 bits, dense count vector) while keeping the rest of the featurizer and the CatBoost model unchanged; the supplied train.py has no random forest, so the CatBoost regressor is the model left in place.

issues: No measurement circumvention: features are computed per-molecule from SMILES only; no file/network access, no hard-coded predictions, no use of test labels.
No correctness bug: the three SMARTS patterns are valid, hand_feats returns a fixed-length vector for every molecule, and the existing nan_to_num still covers the appended columns.

Redundancy / simplicity concern: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, ring counts, aromatic rings, FractionCSP3 and heavy atom count are already present in Descriptors.descList. Only formal charge and the acid / basic-N / quaternary-N counts are genuinely new, so the added code buys little.

Recomputed z (positive = candidate better): (0.3837 - 0.3846) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1 + 1)) = -0.172, consistent with the harness value of -0.162 up to rounding of the reported means. Either way the candidate is not an improvement; reject is the right provisional call.
No claims accompanying the diff contradict the numbers.

description: Append a compact set of 14 hand-picked permeability features (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, H-bond donors/acceptors, rotatable bonds, ring and aromatic ring counts, Fsp3, heavy atoms, formal charge sum, and SMARTS counts for carboxylic acids, basic amines and quaternary/permanent cations) to the existing Morgan count plus RDKit descriptor features.

Swap the CatBoost regressor for LightGBM (LGBMRegressor, objective='l1', 15 leaves, lr 0.03, 600 rounds, feature_fraction 0.5, bagging 0.8 every round) on the existing Morgan-count plus RDKit-descriptor features.

Aborted the "Add RDKit 2D descriptor block" idea: the current train.py already concatenates the full RDKit Descriptors.descList block (NaN/inf-cleaned) with the fingerprint, so the spec would be a near no-op.
Abort the scaffold-grouped random-forest hyperparameter search, because the incumbent model is CatBoost, not a forest, and a tuned RF is unlikely to close the gap.

Replace the single CatBoost model with a stacked ensemble of Morgan-count random forest, LightGBM L1 on counts plus descriptors, and Tanimoto-kernel SVR, blended with nonnegative sum-to-one weights fitted by SLSQP to minimise MAE on scaffold-grouped inner out-of-fold predictions.

Append 30 PCA component scores, fit on training molecules only over standardised descriptors plus Morgan counts, to the CatBoost MAE feature matrix (kept CatBoost rather than switching to LightGBM, since LightGBM was already tested and rejected).

Fit an OLS baseline on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, train the existing CatBoost model on the residuals, and add the linear prediction back for test molecules (applied to the current CatBoost incumbent, since the spec's random forest is no longer in train.py).

Fit an OLS baseline on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, train the existing CatBoost model on the residuals, and add the linear prediction back for test molecules (applied to the current CatBoost incumbent, since the spec's random forest is no longer in train.py).
Abort the ExtraTrees idea: the current train.py has no RandomForestRegressor to replace, and the idea would be another model-family swap that the notes say to avoid.
Replace the Morgan count fingerprint with a feature-invariant (FCFP-like) Morgan count generator at radius 2 with 2048 bins, leaving the CatBoost model and OLS baseline unchanged.
Add 1024 hashed topological-torsion count bins alongside 1024 Morgan count bins in the featurizer, keeping the existing CatBoost model (the file has no random forest to keep).
Average test predictions of an RF on Morgan counts, a LightGBM L1 model on counts plus descriptors, and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR on binary Morgan, with equal weights.

Gaussian-rank transform of the OLS residual target before CatBoost MAE fitting, with np.interp inverse mapping of predictions back to the residual scale (clipped to the training range) before adding back the linear part.

Aborted the Tanimoto-kernel SVR idea: it is a near-duplicate of slot 3 (Tanimoto kernel ridge on binary Morgan fingerprints, official 0.4357, +0.052 vs incumbent), and the notes say family swaps have lost while the OLS-residual plus MAE-CatBoost setup has won.

Aborted the XGBoost absolute-error idea: it swaps the CatBoost regressor for another gradient-boosted L1 tree model, which is a near-duplicate of the LightGBM L1 swap (slot 8, 0.3882, rejected) and the GBR quantile swap (slot 4, 0.3909, rejected).
Abort the seed-averaged LightGBM L1 idea: it is a LightGBM family swap that the notes and slot 8 already show loses to the incumbent.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff adds only per-molecule 3D shape descriptors (PBF, PMI1-3, NPR1-2, radius of gyration). They are computed from each molecule's own SMILES with a fixed embedding seed. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Minor points: (a) EmbedMolecule runs on the molecule without explicit hydrogens, so the geometries are rough. (b) When embedding fails, the shape block is all zeros, which the model cannot tell apart from a real value; a missing-value flag or NaN would be cleaner. (c) Embedding runs again in every fit, which adds runtime, but it is deterministic and should stay well under the 10-minute limit.

Recomputed z = (0.3711 - 0.378) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.0069 / 0.00453 ≈ -1.52. This matches the harness value of -1.517; the small gap comes from rounding of the incumbent mean. The candidate is worse by about 0.007 MAE, so rejecting it is consistent with the numbers.

description: Append 7 three-dimensional shape and planarity descriptors (PBF, PMI1-3, NPR1-2, radius of gyration) from a single ETKDG conformer per molecule, with zeros when embedding fails, to the existing Morgan-plus-descriptor vector before the unchanged CatBoost fit.

Adds an ElasticNetCV linear model on Morgan counts plus standardised RDKit descriptors (constant columns dropped, 5-fold CV seeded) and averages its predictions 50/50 with the existing OLS-plus-CatBoost-residual prediction.

Pass CatBoost monotone_constraints of -1 on the RDKit TPSA, NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors columns (located by name in Descriptors.descList, offset by N_BITS) and 0 elsewhere, keeping the OLS residual setup and MAE CatBoost model unchanged.

Two-stage residual boosting: CatBoost MAE on the OLS residual with 4-fold inner out-of-fold predictions, then a shallower depth-4 CatBoost MAE that corrects the OOF residuals, with predictions summed with the OLS prior.

After the CatBoost MAE fit on the OLS residual target, compute scaffold-grouped inner 4-fold out-of-fold residuals of that boosting model, then add 0.5 times the similarity-weighted mean residual of each test molecule's 5 nearest training neighbours by binary Morgan Tanimoto, skipping molecules whose max similarity is below 0.3.

Add CatBoost regularization for decorrelated trees: rsm=0.3, Bernoulli row subsampling at 0.7, and l2_leaf_reg=10, keeping the MACCS-plus-descriptor features, the OLS residual setup, MAE loss, ITERS and LR unchanged.

Winsorise the training targets by clipping train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles (computed on train_y only) before the OLS baseline and CatBoost residual fit, leaving the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual, but choose a shrink factor alpha from {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2} by scaffold-grouped inner 4-fold out-of-fold MAE of OLS + alpha * residual, then refit CatBoost on all training rows and apply that alpha to the test residuals.

issues: No integrity problems. Scaffold counts and sample weights are computed from train_smiles only. Test inputs are featurized the same way as before, and no labels, files or network are used.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Each weight is 1/sqrt(scaffold count), normalized to mean 1. These are sound per-sample weights for CatBoost, and the linear part (coef) is unchanged. Minor robustness note: MurckoScaffoldSmiles would fail if MolFromSmiles returned None, but that would crash the run, not distort the score.

Recomputed z: the candidate (0.3724) is 0.0013 worse than the incumbent (0.3711). The standard error of the difference is 0.0037*sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00453, so z ≈ -0.29. The reported -0.302 matches within the rounding of the 4-decimal means (a difference of about 0.00137). Lower loss is better, so the candidate is slightly worse, though the gap is within noise. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers. The extra code (2 imports, 4 lines) is also not worth it without a gain.

description: Weights each training molecule by 1/sqrt(its Murcko scaffold count in the training fold, rescaled to mean 1) and passes them as sample_weight to the existing CatBoost MAE fit, so large scaffold series do not dominate the boosting loss.
Adds four SMARTS ionisation-class counts (acids, basic aliphatic amines, permanent cations, phenols) to the OLS prior features only, leaving the CatBoost feature matrix unchanged.

Replace the four-term OLS prior with a Ridge(alpha=1.0) prior on a cubic SplineTransformer basis (4 knots) over TPSA, MolLogP and MolWt plus linear NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors, keeping the CatBoost MAE model on the residual unchanged.

Aborted the median-of-trees idea: the incumbent train.py has no random forest, so there are no per-tree predictions to take a median over, and the closest analogue (per-iteration CatBoost predictions) is not the same estimator.

Keep the OLS prior and residual target, but replace the single CatBoost MAE model with six models (depths 4, 6, 8, each at two seeds, seed and seed+1000, with 1000, 800 and 600 iterations) and return the element-wise median of their residual predictions plus the OLS term.

Divide the Morgan count vector by each molecule's heavy-atom count and append log(heavy-atom count) as one extra column, keeping the RDKit descriptor block, OLS prior and CatBoost MAE model unchanged.

Two-pass CatBoost feature pruning: fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the OLS residual using all Morgan and descriptor columns, keep the top 300 columns by get_feature_importance(), and refit a fresh model with the same settings and seed on the reduced matrix, adding the OLS prior back at prediction time.

Replace the OLS linear prior with a median (L1) QuantileRegressor on standardised TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, fit on training molecules only, and keep the CatBoost MAE model on the prior residual.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels. The MIN_COUNT feature filter is computed from training-fold rows only (X_tr), then applied to both X_tr and X_te, so nothing leaks from the test fold.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Each radius gets its own block of N_BITS columns, so there's no overlap. nfp correctly splits the fingerprint columns from the descriptor columns, and the keep mask always keeps every descriptor column. The residual target (y - A_tr @ coef, with A_te @ coef added back to the predictions) is unchanged from the incumbent.

Recomputed z = (0.3711 - 0.3783) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.0072 / 0.00453 ≈ -1.59. This matches the harness value of -1.591; the small gap comes from rounding the means. The candidate is worse by about 0.007 on a single run, so rejecting it is consistent with the numbers.
Minor point: the change also moves from one radius at 2048 bits to three radii at 1024 bits each. Several changes are bundled in one edit, so we can't tell which one caused the loss to rise.

description: Replace the single radius-2 Morgan count block with count fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 (1024 bits each), drop bits nonzero in fewer than 3 training molecules (filter fit on the training fold only), and keep the OLS prior plus CatBoost MAE pipeline unchanged.

Replace the global OLS prior with a Gaussian-weighted local linear prior (k=100 nearest training molecules in standardised TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP space, self excluded for training rows), then fit CatBoost MAE on the residual and add the local prior back.

Adds a smoothed, out-of-fold Morgan radius-1/2 environment target encoding of the OLS residual as a ridge prior (alpha chosen by inner 5-fold CV) between the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE model; uses unfolded Morgan IDs rather than hashed ones to avoid collisions.

Replace the OLS prior with a ridge model on Nystroem RBF features (300 components, gamma=1/n_features) of standardised RDKit descriptors, and fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the ridge residual.

Aborted the out-of-fold ridge descriptor-embedding idea: the current featurize() already feeds CatBoost every RDKit descriptor, so ridge predictions of those descriptors add little new signal, and it is another feature-stacking variant of the out-of-fold target encoding (slot 34) and PCA (slot 10) edits that lost.

Aborted the out-of-fold Tanimoto kNN feature idea: it is a near-duplicate of slot 34 (out-of-fold Morgan environment target encoding, rejected at 0.3764) and slot 3 (Tanimoto-similarity regression, rejected at 0.4357), and the notes say feature stacking on the OLS-prior CatBoost setup has consistently lost.

Two-phase boosting on the OLS residual: a 400-iteration CatBoost Huber(delta=0.3) model first, then a CatBoost MAE model fit to what the Huber model's in-sample predictions leave behind, with the final prediction the OLS prior plus both models.

Keep the RDKit descriptor block and the 256 Morgan count bits most |Spearman|-correlated with the training-fold OLS residual (computed on training molecules only, constant bits ignored), dropping the rest of the Morgan block, and fit the unchanged CatBoost MAE model on that residual.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers, and test labels are never used. The test molecules only supply features. Both the linear baseline and CatBoost are fit on training data only.

No bugs that would make the result meaningless. Each sub-model uses the same column subset for training and test features. Predictions are fit on the linear-baseline residuals and the baseline A_te @ coef is added back, the same way the incumbent does it. All randomness comes from seed: column sampling through default_rng(seed), and each sub-model gets random_seed=seed*10+i.

Minor style point: the candidate hard-codes depth=5, lr=0.1 and iterations=300 instead of using the DEPTH/LR/ITERS constants. So this changes the hyperparameters and adds a feature-subsampled bagging ensemble in the same edit, which confounds what the result says.

Recomputed z: (0.3711 - 0.3772) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.0061 / 0.00453 ≈ -1.35. This matches the reported -1.356 within rounding of the means. The candidate scores worse than the incumbent (0.3772 vs 0.3711), but the gap is within noise, so rejecting it is consistent. The candidate also adds complexity, which the program card discourages.

description: Replace the single CatBoost residual model with an average of 6 random-subspace CatBoost MAE models (depth 5, 300 iterations, lr 0.1, 40% of feature columns each, Bernoulli row subsampling 0.8) fit on the OLS residual, with the OLS prior added back.

Aborted the generic-scaffold plus side-chain Morgan block idea: it is a near-duplicate of Morgan-variant features that already lost (count fingerprints, FCFP-like, radius mix, torsion bins, per-heavy-atom normalisation), so it is not worth one of the remaining slots.

Append seven Gasteiger partial-charge summaries (positive and negative charge sums, max and min charge, N/O charge-weighted TPSA, count of atoms with |q|>0.2, mean |q|) to the Morgan+RDKit feature vector; the spec says 8 scalars but lists 7, so I implemented the 7 listed.
Replace the four-term OLS prior with a median (L1) QuantileRegressor prior on Crippen atom-type counts plus scaled TPSA and MolWt, keeping CatBoost MAE on the prior residual.

Choose the CatBoost residual iteration count by early stopping on a scaffold-held-out 10% validation split of the training fold, then refit on all training data with 1.1x the best count; this keeps CatBoost instead of the LightGBM family swap the spec names, since slot 8 already rejected LightGBM.

Before fitting, smooth each training target toward the mean of its 5 nearest Tanimoto neighbours (binary Morgan r=2, within the training fold, self excluded) with lam=0.3, then fit the existing OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual model on the smoothed targets.

Append a 1024-bin folded Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pair count fingerprint (Gen2DFingerprint on-bits summed modulo 1024) to the existing featurize() output, leaving the OLS prior, CatBoost MAE residual model and all other settings unchanged.

Keep the OLS prior and residual target, but replace the CatBoost MAE residual model with LightGBM L1 linear-leaf trees (linear_tree=True, linear_lambda=1.0, 15 leaves, lr 0.05, 400 estimators, subsampling) on the same featurized matrix.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only replaces the CatBoost residual model with an LGBMRegressor. It adds no file or network access, pastes in no answers and never uses test labels. The linear baseline is still fit on training data only, and the seed is passed through to the model.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The bad loss of 0.819 against the incumbent's 0.3711 most likely comes from the model choices themselves, so it is a real measurement of a weak model. One likely cause: linear_tree=True fits linear models in each leaf over unscaled, high-dimensional features (fingerprint bits plus descriptors) with only linear_lambda=1.0 regularisation, and those can extrapolate wildly on unseen scaffolds. The other: the objective changed from MAE to L2 ('regression'), while the scoring uses MAE.

Recomputed z: (0.3711 - 0.819) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.4479 / 0.004532 ≈ -98.8. The harness reports -98.208. The small gap is probably rounding of the displayed values or a slightly different noise sd (about 0.00372). Either way the decision is the same.
Rejecting is clearly right: the candidate is about 0.45 worse in MAE, which is more than 100 times the per-job noise sd.

description: LightGBM rejects the regression_l1 objective when linear_tree=True, so I switched the booster objective to the L2 'regression' objective, which linear trees support, and left the rest of the model unchanged.

Fit a 4-fold scaffold-grouped inner loop of the full OLS-plus-CatBoost pipeline to get out-of-fold predictions, fit a two-parameter affine map (a + b*pred) by minimising MAE from a=0, b=1, then refit the pipeline on all training data and apply the map to the test predictions.

Replace the four-term OLS prior with a six-term Abraham-style solvation linear prior (Crippen logP, TPSA, H-bond donors, H-bond acceptors, carboxylic acid count, aliphatic amine count via SMARTS), keeping the CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged.
Aborted the variance-threshold idea: the incumbent has no random forest to feed, and CatBoost already ignores constant bits, so dropping near-constant Morgan columns should change almost nothing.

Gate the CatBoost residual correction by each test molecule's maximum Tanimoto similarity (binary Morgan r=2, 2048 bits) to the training set, using g = clip((maxsim - 0.25) / 0.25, 0, 1) so dissimilar molecules fall back to the pure OLS prior.

Keep the OLS prior and residual target, but fit CatBoost MAE in two stages: a depth-8 model (300 iterations, lr 0.05) followed by a depth-4 model (500 iterations, lr 0.03) continued from it via init_model, both seeded with the harness seed.

Append eight hand-computed ring-topology and linker features (ring-system count, largest fused system size, shared ring bonds, longest non-ring linker, ring-atom fraction, rotatable-bond ratio, ring count, multi-ring atom count) to the featurize() output, leaving the OLS prior and CatBoost settings unchanged.

Average two CatBoost MAE residual models with equal weight: one on the full Morgan-count plus RDKit-descriptor features and one on the descriptor-only columns with a different seed, then add the OLS prior.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The test molecules are only featurized, their labels are never used, and there is no file or network access.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The extra depth-1 CatBoost model is trained on the same training residuals. Its prediction is averaged 50/50 with the main model and added back to the linear baseline, so the result is still valid. The only side effects are slower runs and slightly more code.

z checks out. The candidate's loss is 0.3856 against the incumbent's 0.3711, which is 0.0145 worse. The sd of that difference is 0.0037*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.00453. That gives z ≈ -3.20, against the harness's -3.184. The small gap is most likely from rounding in the shown means. The candidate is clearly worse, so reject is the right call.

description: Fit a second CatBoost MAE model with depth 1 (2000 iterations, lr 0.05) on the same OLS-residual target and average its predictions with the depth-6 model's equally before adding the OLS prior.

Replace the CatBoost residual model with an ARD Matern(2.5) Gaussian process on standardised RDKit descriptors (no Morgan bits), fit on the OLS residual with hyperparameters learned on a 200-molecule subset, and add the OLS prior back.

The timeout came from the GP's ARD Matern kernel, which fits about 200 separate length scales (one per descriptor) and restarts the optimizer, repeated across 15 fits; switching to a single shared length scale keeps the same GP model but cuts the hyperparameter count to about 3, so the job should finish well within 600 s.

Keep the OLS prior and residual target, but average equal-weight predictions from a CatBoost MAE residual model and a CatBoost Huber(delta=0.5) residual model, both with depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations and the same seed.

Append RDKit EState fingerprint count and sum vectors (79 bins each, float32) to the existing Morgan-count and descriptor features in featurize(), leaving the OLS prior and all other settings unchanged.

Train the CatBoost MAE residual model in four warm-started 300-iteration segments (init_model chaining) with learning rate cosine-decayed from 0.08 to 0.01, keeping the OLS prior, residual target and features.

Replace the OLS prior with a Tukey-biweight IRLS robust linear fit (10 steps, scale from MAD, c=4.685) on the four-term TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP prior, keeping the CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged.
Add CatBoost random_strength=2.0 and Bayesian bootstrap (bagging_temperature=1.0) to the existing OLS-prior plus CatBoost MAE residual model, with no other changes.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Test labels are never used. The standardization mean and sd, the OLS fits, the pairwise-product OLS and the Huber fit all use training data only. Test molecules only get transformed with those fitted values.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The averaged prior is computed the same way on train and test. CatBoost is fit on the training residuals and the prior is added back at prediction time. The seed is passed through. Note: np.triu_indices includes the diagonal, so the squared terms are in the model too. That is fine, but the comment does not mention it.

The numbers support the reject. The candidate scores 0.3731 against the incumbent mean of 0.3711, so it is 0.0020 worse. Using the noise sd of 0.0037, the standard error of the difference is 0.0037*sqrt(1/1+1/2) = 0.00453. That gives z ≈ -0.44, which matches the harness's -0.445 up to rounding of the reported means. The extra prior code adds complexity and does not improve the score.

description: Replace the single OLS prior with the average of three linear priors (OLS on the four terms, OLS on the four terms plus pairwise products, and a Huber fit with epsilon=1.35), averaging their predictions, and keep the CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged.

Replace the OLS prior with an MAE-fitted (QuantileRegressor, median) prior on TPSA and MolLogP hinge bases at training 25/50/75th percentile knots, plus linear MolWt and NumHDonors, and keep the CatBoost MAE model on the residuals.

Replace the four-term OLS prior with sklearn ARDRegression fit on standardised RDKit descriptors plus the four base features (training fold only), keeping the CatBoost MAE residual model and adding the prior back at prediction time.

Clip each RDKit descriptor column to the training fold's 1st and 99th percentiles, then standardise with training-fold mean and SD, applying the same bounds and statistics to test molecules, while leaving the Morgan counts and target unchanged; the OLS prior still uses unclipped base features.

Replace the four-term OLS prior with an OLS prior on the RDKit descriptors plus base features that LassoCV selects in at least 60% of 50 random half-subsamples of the training fold, keeping the existing CatBoost MAE residual model.
Remove the unsupported n_alphas keyword from LassoCV, which this scikit-learn version rejects, so LassoCV falls back to its default alpha grid.
Abort the untrained random-weight message-passing embedding idea: it would append a 48-dim pooled feature block, the same kind of feature stacking that has been rejected repeatedly.

Replace the four-term OLS prior with a LassoCV prior on 14 standardised polynomial terms (4 linear, 4 squares, 6 pairwise products) of TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, and fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the residual.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The bins, the bootstrap indices and the OLS coefficients all come only from train_smiles and train_y. Test molecules are only featurized and predicted. All randomness uses the seed argument (RandomState(seed), random_seed=seed+b).

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Stratified bootstrap bagging of the CatBoost residual model is valid. Empty strata are filtered out. The OLS baseline is added back once to the mean of the 5 bags.

z is consistent. Difference = 0.3711 - 0.3855 = -0.0144. Standard error for one candidate run against the mean of 2 incumbent runs = 0.0037*sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00453, so z ≈ -3.18. That matches the harness's -3.170 up to rounding of the reported means. The candidate is clearly worse, so reject is the right call.

Minor note: the job now trains 5 CatBoost models per fold, so it costs about 5 times the compute for a worse loss. Bagging probably reduces the effective sample size and adds variance in this small-data setting.

description: Replace the single CatBoost residual model with 5 CatBoost MAE models, each trained on a stratified bootstrap that resamples every quantile bin of the OLS residual with replacement, then average their predictions and add the OLS prior back.

Replace the CatBoost MAE residual model with a CatBoost RMSE model on the OLS residual, and add a median offset m, estimated from 4-fold scaffold-grouped out-of-fold residuals, to the test predictions.

Replace the single CatBoost MAE residual fit with a two-pass scheme: fit the MAE model, then refit an RMSE CatBoost on the same OLS residual target, with rows weighted by a Cauchy redescending weight 1/(1+(res/c)^2) where c is 1.4826 times the median absolute residual.

Aborted the multi-conformer 3D descriptor idea: it is a near-duplicate of rejected slot 17 (single-conformer 3D shape descriptors, 0.3780), the notes say to avoid new feature blocks, and 10 ETKDG+MMFF conformers per molecule across 15 fits risks the 10-minute job limit.

issues: No numbers yet (no run after the lint repair), so z can't be computed.
Re-converting each fragment to SMILES is mostly redundant; the fragmenter's output is already canonical.
The character-sum bin assignment repeats exactly, but different fragments will often land in the same bin, which adds noise. This is harmless to the measurement.
Fragmenting large molecules can be slow and adds feature time on every fold. It should still fit in the 10-minute limit.
It adds about 20 lines of code; only worth keeping if the gain clearly beats the noise (sd 0.0037).

description: Appends a 512-bin crc32-hashed count vector of BRICS fragment canonical SMILES to each molecule's existing Morgan-count plus RDKit-descriptor features, leaving the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged.

Replace the 2048-bit Morgan radius-2 count block in featurize() with a 1024-bin Avalon count fingerprint (GetAvalonCountFP), keeping the RDKit descriptor block, the four-term OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged.

Average equal-weight test predictions from three CatBoost MAE residual models (same OLS prior), each trained on a different Morgan count variant: radius 2 without chirality, radius 2 with useChirality=True, and radius 3, each 2048-bin hashed and with RDKit descriptors computed once and shared.

Adds 30 pairwise product and ratio features built from the six RDKit descriptors most Spearman-correlated with the OLS residual on the training fold, keeping the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual model.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The kNN residual term uses only training residuals (resid = y - A_tr @ coef). The winsorising percentiles and the standardisation statistics come from the training rows only. Test molecules contribute features only, never labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The squared-distance expansion is correct, and with 15 neighbours the median of the training residuals is well defined. The fixed 0.75/0.25 blend is a hand-picked constant, not tuned on test folds.

The numbers agree with the decision. The candidate scored 0.379 against the incumbent's 0.3711, so it is worse by 0.0079. Using a per-run sd of 0.0037, the standard error of the difference is 0.0037*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.00453, which gives |z| ≈ 1.74. That matches the reported -1.745 under the harness sign convention, where negative means the candidate is worse. Rejecting is correct.
Minor point: the candidate has only 1 run. It is worse by about 1.7 SE, so a replicate is unlikely to reverse the decision, and the added code would not be worth it anyway under the simplicity rule.

description: Blend a descriptor-space kNN median of the OLS residuals (k=15, standardised winsorised RDKit descriptors) with the CatBoost residual prediction at 0.25/0.75 weights, then add the OLS term.

Append six SMARTS-based intramolecular hydrogen-bond and shielded-polarity counts (amide NH to carbonyl at one and two bonds, NH to a carbon-attached acceptor, ortho-phenol OH to carbonyl or nitrogen, and unmasked N/O atom count) to each molecule's feature vector, leaving the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

Aborted the backfitted MAE additive spline prior idea: it is a near-duplicate of rejected slot 27 (cubic spline basis prior, 0.3732) and of the other rejected fancier-prior swaps, so it is unlikely to beat the incumbent beyond noise.

Add langevin=True and diffusion_temperature=1000 to the existing CatBoost MAE residual model so its regularisation comes from injected SGLB noise, keeping the OLS prior, depth, learning rate, iterations and seed unchanged.

Aborted the heteroatom topological-distance pair histogram idea: it would append about 48 sparse integer columns to a feature set that already exceeds 2,000 columns, and every comparable topology or feature-block addition in the log (torsion, Gobbi, BRICS, 3D shape, EState, ring topology) was rejected within noise.

Replace the CatBoost MAE residual model with a LightGBM DART L1 regressor (drop_rate 0.1, skip_drop 0.5, 400 rounds, lr 0.05, 15 leaves, feature and bagging fractions 0.5 and 0.8) fit on the same OLS-prior residual target, seeded by the harness seed.

Replace the CatBoost residual model with a 300-tree RandomForest (min_samples_leaf=3, max_features=0.3) on the OLS residual, and predict each test molecule's residual as the leaf-size-weighted median of training residuals that share leaves with it.

Pairwise difference learning: a CatBoost MAE model is trained on OLS-prior residual differences between each training molecule and its 10 nearest Tanimoto neighbours, and test predictions average the anchor residuals plus the learned difference, added back to the OLS prior.
